Rashi on Yevamot 21a:10:1.english: Avoid it [pera'ehu] - Make it grow as a prohibition and add to it, so that you do not transgress it; [this is] like "let [the hair] grow long [gaddel pera]" [Numbers 6:5].

Rashi on Yevamot 21a:12:1.english: And you shall keep My charge - [It] is written regarding forbidden relationships.

Rashi on Yevamot 21a:14:1.hebrew: אם אמו - אמו כתיבא, וגזרו רבנן על אם אמו כדי שלא יפגע באמו. וגזרו נמי באם אביו משום אם אמו, ואע"ג דגזירה לגזירה הוא, כדאמר לקמן, משום דתרוייהו "אימא רבתא" קרו להו:
Rashi on Yevamot 21a:14:1.english: His mother's mother - His mother is written [in the Torah], and the Rabbis decreed [a prohibition] on his mother's mother so that he will not stumble [into sin] with his mother. And they also decreed [a prohibition] on his father's mother because of his mother's mother, even though it is a decree upon a decree, as [the Gemara] says later, because both of them are called "grandmother."

Rashi on Yevamot 21a:14:2.english: And his father's father's wife - [She is prohibited] because of his father's wife, which is written [in the Torah].

Rashi on Yevamot 21a:14:3.hebrew: ואשת אבי אמו - ואע"ג דאשת אבי (אם) אמו גזירה משום אשת אבי אביו, דתרוייהו אבא רבא קרו להו, והילכך חדא הוא:
Rashi on Yevamot 21a:14:3.english: And his mother’s father’s wife - And even though [the prohibition of] his mother’s father’s wife is a decree on account of his father’s father’s wife [— making it a decree upon a decree — nevertheless it was decreed], for both of them are called “grandfather” (abba rabba), and therefore it is [considered] one [category].

Rashi on Yevamot 21a:14:4.hebrew: ואשת אחי האב מן האם - דמן התורה "ערות אחי אביך" כתיב, ואמרינן לקמן בהבא על יבמתו דבאחי אביו מן האב קמשתעי. אבל אם היה אחיו של אביו מן האם, שריא, וגזרו רבנן עלה משום אשת אחי אביו מן האב:
Rashi on Yevamot 21a:14:4.english: And the wife of his father’s maternal [half] brother - For by Torah law, "the nakedness of your father’s brother" is written, and we say later in [the chapter] Haba Al Yevimto that [Scripture] speaks of his father’s paternal [half] brother. However, if he was his father’s maternal [half] brother, she is permitted [by Torah law], and the Sages decreed against her on account of the wife of his father’s paternal [half] brother.

Rashi on Yevamot 21a:14:5.hebrew: ואשת אחי האם מן האב - כגון נפתלי אחי יוכבד מאביה ונשא אשה, אסורה לאהרן משום שניה, דאע"ג דאשת אחי אמו לא כתיבא, גזרו בה רבנן היכא דהוא אחי אמו מן האב, גזירה משום אחי אביו מן האם דהויא נמי שנייה ואיכא צד אב. אבל אם היה נפתלי אחי יוכבד מן האם ולא מן האב, מיבעי לקמן בגמרא אי גזור רבנן עלה אי לאו:
Rashi on Yevamot 21a:14:5.english: And the wife of his mother's paternal [half] brother - For example, Naftali was Yocheved's brother from her father and married a woman; [that woman] is forbidden to Aaron [Yocheved's son] as a secondary [prohibited relationship]. For even though the wife of one's mother's brother is not written [in the Torah], the Sages decreed regarding her where he is his mother's brother from the father, as a decree on account of [the wife of] his father's brother from the mother, which is also a secondary [prohibited relationship] and involves a paternal side. However, if Naftali was Yocheved's brother from the mother and not from the father, it is asked later in the Gemara whether the Sages decreed regarding her or not.

Rashi on Yevamot 21a:14:6.english: And his son's daughter-in-law - [The Sages] decreed [this prohibition] because of his [own] daughter-in-law.

Rashi on Yevamot 21a:14:7.hebrew: וכלת בתו - מפרש טעמא לקמן, גזירה משום כלת בנו:
Rashi on Yevamot 21a:14:7.english: And his daughter’s daughter-in-law - [The Gemara] explains the reason later: [it is] a decree on account of his son’s daughter-in-law.

Rashi on Yevamot 21a:14:9.hebrew: ואסור בבת חורגו - לקמן פריך: הא דאורייתא היא, "את בת בנה", ואמאי תני לה בהדי שניות:
Rashi on Yevamot 21a:14:9.english: And he is prohibited from [marrying] the daughter of his stepson - Later, [the Gemara] asks: [Surely] this is [prohibited] by Torah law — "her son's daughter" [Leviticus 18:17] — and why does [the baraita] teach it together with the secondary [relationships]?

Rashi on Yevamot 21a:17:1.english: This is conclusive for him - His stepson's daughter is forever forbidden to him.

Rashi on Yevamot 21a:17:2.hebrew: הא לא פסיקא ליה - בת אשת חמיו האסורה לו משום אחות אשה, הואיל ולאחר מיתת אשתו מותרת לו, לא פסיקא ליה:
Rashi on Yevamot 21a:17:2.english: This is not conclusive for him - The daughter of his father-in-law's wife, who is forbidden to him on account of [being] a wife's sister — since after his wife's death she is permitted to him, [this case] is not conclusive for him.

Rashi on Yevamot 21a:18:1.hebrew: ד' נשים שניות יש להן הפסק - שלמעלה מהן ולמטה מהן מותר. אבל האחרות, כגון אם אמו, אין להם הפסק, שלמעלה הימנה עד סוף כל הדורות הויא נמי שנייה. וכן אשת אבי אביו ואם אבי אביו, למעלה מהן עד לעולם אסור, כגון אשת אבי אבי אביו ואם אבי אבי אביו:
Rashi on Yevamot 21a:18:1.english: Four women [who are] secondary [relatives] have a conclusion - [Meaning] that [those] above them and below them are permitted. However, the others, such as his mother's mother, do not have a conclusion, for [any generation] above her until the end of all generations is also a secondary [relative]. And similarly, the wife of his father's father and the mother of his father's father — [generations] above them forever are forbidden, such as the wife of his father's father's father and the mother of his father's father's father.

Rashi on Yevamot 21a:18:2.hebrew: ונקיט רב בידיה תלת - לפרושי תלת מהנך ארבעה, אבל רביעית לא הוה ידע מה היא, אבל גמרא הוה גמיר דארבע נינהו:
Rashi on Yevamot 21a:18:2.english: And Rav held three in his hand - To specify three of those four, but [as for] the fourth, he did not know what it was; however, he had learned by tradition that there are four.

Rashi on Yevamot 21a:18:3.hebrew: אשת אחי האם מן האב - היא לבדה שנייה, אבל אשת אחי אם אמו מותרת:
Rashi on Yevamot 21a:18:3.english: The wife of his mother's paternal [half] brother - She alone is a secondary [forbidden relationship], but the wife of the brother of his mother's mother is permitted.

Rashi on Yevamot 21a:18:4.hebrew: ואשת אחי האב מן האם - לבדה שנייה, אבל אשת אחי אבי אביו מן האם מותרת. וטעמא, משום דלא שייכא בהו ערוה דאורייתא. אבל אם אמו, דשייכא בדורותיה ערוה דאורייתא — כגון אמו — אין לה הפסק; ואשת אבי אביו, יש בדורותיה אשת אב דאורייתא; ואם אביו נמי, אע"ג דלא שייכא בדורה ערוה דאורייתא, אין לה הפסק, ואסורה אף אם אבי אביו, דמיחלפא באם אם אמו:
Rashi on Yevamot 21a:18:4.english: And the wife of his father’s maternal brother - she alone is a secondary [forbidden relationship], but the wife of his father’s father’s maternal brother is permitted. And the reason is because no biblically forbidden relationship applies in their [generations]. However, his mother’s mother, in whose generations a biblically forbidden relationship applies — such as his mother — [has no conclusion]; and the wife of his father’s father has in her generations [the prohibition of] a father’s wife, [which is] biblically [forbidden]; and his father’s mother as well, even though no biblically forbidden relationship applies in her generation, has no conclusion, and even his father’s father’s mother is forbidden, because she might be confused with his mother’s mother’s mother.

Rashi on Yevamot 21a:18:5.hebrew: וכלתו - יש לה הפסק. ולקמן פריך: היכי חשיב כלתו בהדי שניות? הא דאורייתא היא! ומתרץ: אימא כלת בתו, דחשבינן לה לעיל בשניות, וקאמר רב דיש לה הפסק הואיל ולא שייכא בה איסור כלה דאורייתא. הילכך, כלת בת בתו שריא; אבל כלת בנו אין לה הפסק, וכלת בן בנו נמי אסירא, הואיל ושייכא בדורות הללו איסור כלה דאורייתא:
Rashi on Yevamot 21a:18:5.english: And his daughter-in-law - [She] has a conclusion. And later [the Gemara] asks: How can he count his daughter-in-law among the secondary [forbidden relationships]? Surely she is [forbidden] by Torah law! And [it] answers: Say [instead], "the daughter-in-law of his daughter," whom we counted above among the secondary [forbidden relationships]; and Rav is saying that [she] has a conclusion since the Torah prohibition of a daughter-in-law does not apply to her. Therefore, the daughter-in-law of his daughter's daughter is permitted; however, the daughter-in-law of his son has no conclusion, and the daughter-in-law of his son's son is also forbidden, since the Torah prohibition of a daughter-in-law applies in these generations.

Rashi on Yevamot 21a:18:6.hebrew: אשת אבי אמו - יש לה הפסק, ושרינן אשת אבי אבי אמו, הואיל ולא שייכא בדורות הללו אישות אב דאורייתא:
Rashi on Yevamot 21a:18:6.english: The wife of his mother's father - [This prohibition] has a cutoff, and we permit the wife of his mother's father's father, since a father's marital relationship by Torah law does not apply in these generations.

Rashi on Yevamot 21a:18:7.hebrew: וסימן - הא דאוסיף זעירי, דעילאי דרב הוא — דור אחד למעלה משניות דרב, דחשיב אשת אחי האם, וזו של זעירי דור אחד למעלה:
Rashi on Yevamot 21a:18:7.english: And a mnemonic - [for] that which Ze'eiri added: it is "that which is above Rav's" — one generation above the secondary [prohibited relationships] of Rav, for [Rav] counted the wife of the mother's brother, whereas this one of Ze'eiri is one generation above.

Rashi on Yevamot 21a:19:1.hebrew: אשת אבי אמו מחלפא באשת אבי אביו - דאי אמרת יש לה הפסק, אתי למימר באשת אבי אביו יש לה הפסק, והתם איכא באותם דורות אישות דאורייתא:
Rashi on Yevamot 21a:19:1.english: The wife of his mother's father is confused with the wife of his father's father - For if you say [that] it has a limit, one will come to say [that] for the wife of his father's father [as well] there is a limit, whereas there, in those generations, there is a Torah-level marital bond.

Rashi on Yevamot 21a:20:1.hebrew: התם שכיח דאזיל - למשפחת אביו אדם רגיל לילך, ויודע שיש שם קורבה יותר מאמו; הילכך, לא מיחלפי:
Rashi on Yevamot 21a:20:1.english: There he is commonly found to go - A person is accustomed to go to his father's family, and he knows that there is kinship there more than [with] his mother['s family]; therefore, they will not be confused.

Rashi on Yevamot 21a:4:1.hebrew: כי את כל התועבות האל - גבי עריות כתיב, ומשמע התועבות הקשות:
Rashi on Yevamot 21a:4:1.english: For all these abominations - [This] is written regarding forbidden relations, and it implies the harsh abominations.

Rashi on Yevamot 21a:4:2.english: By inference that there are soft ones - [Ones] lighter than them, and [they are] forbidden.

Rashi on Yevamot 21a:6:1.hebrew: אלה - במדות כתיב: "כי תועבת ה' כל עושה אלה כל עושה עול", ומדקאמר "יותר משל עריות", מכלל דהא לאו קשה הוא:
Rashi on Yevamot 21a:6:1.english: These [eleh] - Regarding [dishonest] measures it is written: "For all who do these [eleh], all who do unrighteousness, are an abomination to the Lord." And from the fact that he says "more than that of forbidden relationships," it follows that this [word, el,] is not harsh.

Rashi on Yevamot 21a:7:1.english: Is it not written, “these” - “[For whosoever shall do] any of these abominations ... shall be cut off.”

Rashi on Yevamot 21a:7:2.english: And we ask: If not for a gezerah shavah [verbal analogy], would I have thought [that karet applies] there literally? - [This is asked] in astonishment:

Rashi on Yevamot 21a:8:1.hebrew: עריות אפשר בתקנה - כל זמן שלא הוליד ממזר, יפרוש הימנה ויתחרט; אבל מדות, גזל את הרבים הוא ואינו יודע למי יחזיר, ואע"ג דקיימא לן יתקן בהם צרכי רבים, לאו תשובה מעלייתא הוא:
Rashi on Yevamot 21a:8:1.english: Forbidden relations can be rectified - As long as he has not fathered a mamzer, he can separate from her and feel remorse; but [in the case of dishonest] measures, it is robbery from the public and he does not know to whom to return [it], and even though it is established for us [as law that] he should provide for public needs with them, it is not a proper repentance.

Rashi on Yevamot 21a:9:1.hebrew: ואזן - לשון אזנים, בית אחיזה, כדאמר בעירובין: "לימד דעת את העם" — דאגמרה בסימני טעמא, ואסברה בדדמי, גמר מילתא ממילתא. והזהיר על דברי סופרים, כדכתיב: "ויותר מהמה בני הזהר" — הזהר בדברי סופרים יותר מדברי תורה, וגזר על השניות:
Rashi on Yevamot 21a:9:1.english: And he weighed [ve'izzen] - [This is] an expression of "ears" [oznayim], a handle, as it says in [tractate] Eruvin: "He taught knowledge to the people" — that he taught it with mnemonic signs, and explained it through analogy, deriving one matter from another. And he warned regarding the words of the Scribes, as it is written: "And furthermore, my son, be admonished" — be more careful with the words of the Scribes than with the words of the Torah — and he decreed regarding the secondary [forbidden relationships].

Rashi on Yevamot 21a:9:2.hebrew: אזנים - של קופה, לאחוז בהן הקופה ומשתמרת שלא תפול. ה"נ, ע"י שניות מתרחקין מן העריות:
Rashi on Yevamot 21a:9:2.english: Handles - Of a basket, to hold the basket by them, and [thereby] it is guarded so that it does not fall. So too, through secondary [forbidden relationships], [people] distance themselves from the [biblically] forbidden relationships.

Tosafot on Yevamot 21a:14:1.hebrew: ומותר באשת חמיו - ירושלמי: אשת חמיו אסורה משום מראית העין. וא"ת: תורה היא לאסור'? הא דוד נשא רצפה בת איה! וקאמר נמי: שני חורגין שגדלו בבית — אסורה מפני מראית העין; רבי חנינא אומר: יסבון באתרא דלא חכימי להו. ומעשה בפרובינציא באחד שהיה טבחו טבוח ויינו מזוג לישא אשת חמיו, ואפסדיה ר"ת לסעודתיה. ואע"ג דשמעתין שרי להו אשת חמיו וחורגו, שמא אחר כך אסרום. ומיהו בסוף משוח מלחמה מוכיח סוגיא דלא חיישינן למראית העין גבי חורגה הגדילה בין האחין:
Tosafot on Yevamot 21a:14:1.english: And [a man] is permitted [to marry] his father-in-law's wife - [In the] Jerusalem Talmud [it states]: One's father-in-law's wife is prohibited because of the appearance of impropriety. And if you say [that] it is Torah [law] to prohibit her — behold, David married Ritzpah daughter of Aiah! And it also says: Two step-siblings who grew up in the [same] house — she is prohibited [to him] because of the appearance of impropriety; Rabbi Chanina says: Let them marry in a place where they are not known. And there was an incident in Provence involving a certain man whose animal was slaughtered and whose wine was mixed [in preparation] to marry his father-in-law's wife, and Rabbeinu Tam spoiled his feast [by forbidding it]. And even though our passage permits them — [both] his father-in-law's wife and his stepson's [wife] — perhaps afterwards they prohibited them. However, at the end of [the chapter] Mashuach Milchamah, the sugya proves that we are not concerned about the appearance of impropriety with regard to a stepdaughter who grew up among the brothers.

Tosafot on Yevamot 21a:17:1.hebrew: אי הכי אשת חמיו נמי - מאם אם חמיו לא מצי למיפרך דתימא ליה "אני מותרת לך כו'", דבעיא היא לקמן אם שניות דרבי חייא יש להן הפסק או לא:
Tosafot on Yevamot 21a:17:1.english: If so, his father-in-law’s wife also - From [the case of] the mother of the mother of his father-in-law, [the Gemara] could not object that she should say to him, "I am permitted to you, etc.", because it is an unresolved question later whether the secondary forbidden relatives of Rabbi Chiyya have a limit or not.

Tosafot on Yevamot 21a:9:1.hebrew: רב יהודה אמר ואזן וחקר - והא דאמר בפרק שני דעירובין: "בשעה שתיקן שלמה נטילת ידים ועירובין יצאת בת קול ואמרה כו'", ולא חשיב שניות — שמא אחר בת קול תקנה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 21a:9:1.english: Rav Yehuda said: "He weighed and sought out" - And [regarding] that which [the Gemara] states in the second chapter of Eruvin: "At the time Solomon instituted [the laws of] handwashing and eruvin, a heavenly voice [bat kol] went forth and said, etc.," and it does not count secondary forbidden relationships [sheniyot] — perhaps he instituted it after the heavenly voice.
